name: Logo Intro Sting
summary: The brand mark or wordmark resolves at the centre of a clean background, often with a product line or tagline, and holds briefly before handing off to the first idea. It opens the video and tells the viewer whose story this is.
when_to_use: As the cold open or first beat of a launch or explainer video
When the narration opens by naming the product
As a short brand moment before cutting into the product interface

slots.name: logo
slots.what: the brand mark or wordmark as a vector

slots.name: product_line
slots.what: a product name or short subline under the logo

slots.name: tagline
slots.what: one short claim that follows the logo

slots.name: background
slots.what: a solid colour, a soft gradient or near-black

slots.name: decoration
slots.what: light accents such as drifting bands, sparkles or a faint grid

slots.name: handoff_element
slots.what: the first piece of interface or layout that leads into the next scene

steps: Start on the empty background, or fade up from dark
Resolve the logo: assemble it from fragments, wipe it on, draw its stroke or fade it up
Fade or slide in the product line or tagline under it
Hold the lockup briefly while the narration names the product
Hand off by blurring the logo out, reframing it into a page or interface, or zooming through

build.gsap: One timeline per scene. Resolve the logo with a clip-path wipe, a stroke-dashoffset draw or a staggered gather of fragments into place, using a power or expo out ease; fade the subline up in parallel. Hold, then either tween blur and opacity on the logo while the next layer fades in, or tween the container's scale and position to reframe it into the next layout.
build.remotion: A Sequence for the logo with a spring driving scale or a clip reveal and interpolate for opacity; a nested Sequence starts the subline or tagline after the logo settles; a closing Sequence overlaps the next scene and interpolates blur and opacity for the handoff.

sound: Mostly music and mixed accents. A reverse swoosh building into the logo is the most common clear cue, landing in the middle of the scene; a soft chime can mark the lockup, and an impact sometimes hits late as the handoff begins.
caveats: First-motion timing comes from only a few shots and has a wide spread.
Many sound cues are labelled unsure, and each specific cue type comes from only a few videos.
